author: high3
claim: Let \(p\) be a prime and let \(G\) be a finite group of order \(p^n\) for some integer \(n\ge 1\). Prove that the order of the center \(Z(G)\) is divisible by \(p\), and hence that \(Z(G)\) contains a nonidentity element.

verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. It establishes the orbit-centralizer formula for conjugacy classes, shows that every conjugacy class of a noncentral element has size divisible by p, and applies the class equation to conclude that p divides |Z(G)|. Since the identity lies in Z(G) and p is at least 2, the center contains a nonidentity element. The statement is self-contained, all stated hypotheses are used, and no critical errors, gaps, prohibited justification patterns, internal fact references, or external-paper citations occur.
